clue.text: That's not possible, Bob, love, outside of prison

indicators.note: the bob-and-love letters sit outside, wrapping the word for prison

parts.note: to bob your head is to nod
can is slang for prison
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a jailed friend: sorry Bob, love, but from outside prison there is nothing to be done.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a name addressed in the surface; here it is the verb meaning to nod.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial refusal is an idiom declaring a request impossible to fulfil.

clue.text: Flipping Yelland and his pointless rag exposed

indicators.note: flipping turns the combined letters over, end to end

parts.note: David Yelland edited The Sun, so he is an editor, ED

indicators.note: the paper's name loses its compass point, the S for south

parts.note: his rag is The Sun, the tabloid he edited

explanation.surface: An angry jab at Sun editor David Yelland and his topless-model tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nude is to be naked, uncovered or exposed to view, as Page 3 models were.

clue.text: Take part of corrupt MEP in bed with European head

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A sleazy Euro-MP caught in bed with a European bigwig.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to participate in a contest or race.

clue.text: Sloppy, climax-releasing boudoir habit not without guts

indicators.note: the climax of a word is its last letter, which is let go

parts.note: a negligee is a flimsy dressing gown worn in the bedroom

indicators.note: the word loses its insides, keeping just its outer letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters stay

explanation.surface: A lingerie item undone at the moment of climax, with no guts about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' means a garment, as in a nun's habit, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means careless or failing to take proper care, a close synonym of slapdash.

clue.text: Member put in another bed — initial success if heart, say, is in the right place?

definitions.text: initial success if heart, say, is in the right place?

parts.note: an organ is a part or member of the body
to transplant is to move a plant to a new flowerbed

explanation.surface: An MP hopping into someone else's bed, excused because his heart is in the right place.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves suggest an adulterous member of parliament; the definition literally describes surgery that works at first if the heart sits where it should.
explanation.definitionFit: The operation moves a donor's heart or kidney into a patient, and early success depends on correct placement.

clue.text: Sex urge at first makes you intellectual

indicators.note: the urge word is placed at the front, before the sex word

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
head is slang for oral sex

explanation.surface: A claim that sex drive is what makes a person clever.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sex urge' as a compound and the parse fails; the two words are separate pieces, with the second going first.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal, slightly mocking word for a highbrow, bookish person.

clue.text: Choice oath increasingly heard from the politician these days

definitions.text: increasingly heard from the politician these days

parts.note: an election is a choice made by voters
a promise is a solemn vow, like an oath

explanation.surface: Politicians swearing more and more as the vote approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in the run-up to the June 2001 UK general election.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledges made to voters during a campaign multiply as polling day nears.

clue.text: Walk round in a flaccid state in important company

indicators.note: the walk word goes round the slack word, enclosing it

parts.note: to go is to walk or travel
lax means slack or loose

explanation.surface: A man walking around limp, in the company of important people.
explanation.walkthrough: Glaxo is the British drug giant, merged into GlaxoSmithKline in 2000, makers of medicines for the limp.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaxo was one of Britain's biggest pharmaceutical firms, a major corporation.

clue.text: Altogether unseemly enema straddling a vessel

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit astride the ship, one part either side
unseemly means improper, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An improper enema given while sitting astride a container, in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altogether' hints at 'in the altogether', meaning naked; it simply means all together.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase en masse means all together, as a single group.

clue.text: Brown and all that foreign money shit

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
G is American slang for a grand, a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A jibe at Chancellor Gordon Brown and the foreign cash, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was Chancellor of the Exchequer in 2001; here 'Brown' is just the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dung is animal excrement, manure, a direct synonym of the vulgar noun.

clue.text: Clinton type, keen on uninhibited head and ecstasy — the common folks' leader

parts.note: Bill Clinton is a Democrat, shortened to Dem
agog means eagerly keen

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton, fond of uninhibited oral sex and drugs, portrayed as a man of the people.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the usual crossword abbreviation for the drug ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagogue is a leader who wins power by appealing to the prejudices of ordinary people.

clue.text: Management despot's caught dead short

indicators.note: the despot's name has caught, and so holds, the short form of dead

parts.note: Idi Amin was the Ugandan dictator; 's stands for 'has'
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A tyrannical boss has been caught short and dropped dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin is the everyday shortening of administration, the running and organising of an outfit.

clue.text: What Mandelson's getting good at — accepting the inevitable sponsorship capital?

parts.note: resignation is the calm acceptance of what cannot be changed

indicators.note: a capital is an initial letter, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Peter Mandelson learning to accept his fate over a sponsorship scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mandelson left the Cabinet twice, the second time in 2001 over a passport for a Hinduja brother, whose family sponsored the Millennium Dome.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandelson quit government twice in three years, so stepping down from office was a practised skill.

clue.text: Egg on jug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to provoke, rouse or incite
second meaning: both words are old slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to provoke or rouse people and is also old slang for a prison or jail.

clue.text: Mandy lacks interior regard? Bollocks!

indicators.note: the name loses its middle letters, keeping just its two ends

parts.note: only its first and last letters stay
to eye something is to regard it

explanation.surface: Mandelson, nicknamed Mandy, shown no inner respect, and an expletive in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Mandy is Private Eye's nickname for Peter Mandelson; here it is simply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is an old exclamation of disbelief, a milder way of calling something nonsense.

clue.text: Spot the undercover type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small dark blemish on the skin
second meaning: a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a blemish on the skin and a secret agent planted within an enemy organisation.

clue.text: Short jumpers on the First Lady (large) start to titillate the president

parts.note: roos is the short form of kangaroos, famous jumpers
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A first lady in short frocks setting out to excite the president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short jumpers' suggests cropped sweaters; it is shortened kangaroos. The First Lady is Eve, not a president's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Theodore Roosevelt were both US presidents.

clue.text: Arse up, on Ecstasy, pissed is not how Hague sees us

definitions.text: is not how Hague sees us

indicators.note: pissed means drunk, so these letters stagger out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken, drugged reveller falling over, unlike Hague's tidy vision of the British.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague, Tory leader in 2001, campaigned to keep Britain apart from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurosceptic Hague saw the British as a separate nation rather than citizens of the Continent.

clue.text: Give relief on having an erection, then unstiffen

parts.note: to lighten a burden is to give relief from it
up is slang for being aroused

explanation.surface: A sequence of arousal and relief described with mock delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is to relax and stop being so rigid or serious.

clue.text: Be an egg and have some rumpy-pumpy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an egg is something that gets laid
second meaning: slang for having sex

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase is what happens to an egg from a hen; colloquially it means to have sex.

clue.text: Stuff received

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, British slang for having sex with someone, like stuff
second meaning: the radio reply meaning message received

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a coarse British slang verb for sex and the radio reply confirming a message has arrived.

clue.text: Description of Brenda's mate makes one cringe

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new word, a rearrangement

parts.note: one gives A, the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: Prince Philip's notorious gaffes make people wince.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen; her husband Prince Philip was born a prince of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means Greek in style or origin, fitting the Greek-born royal consort.

clue.text: "TV sound on quick, Brenda!" — studio aid

indicators.note: the TV word is given by how it is said, spelt the short way

parts.note: telly is the British informal word for television
prompt means quick or without delay
Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone shouting at the Queen to turn the television sound up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleprompter scrolls a script for presenters to read on camera, a standard television studio device.

clue.text: "Topless artist breaks up Little and Large — true!"

indicators.note: the artist's letters break into the pair, splitting it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for little, as in clothing sizes

indicators.note: the artist loses his top, the first letter

parts.note: Goya was the Spanish painter

explanation.surface: Comedy duo Little and Large split by a topless model, and it's true.
explanation.walkthrough: Little and Large were a British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means faithful, as a true friend stays steadfast.

clue.text: Bonk (or perhaps you'd prefer smoke)?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: both words are British slang for sex

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket offers a cigarette instead of sex, the old after-sex joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for having sex and also names a strong shredded pipe tobacco.

clue.text: A leader's no leader, getting the sweats

indicators.note: the leader's name loses its leading letter

parts.note: William Hague was leader of the Conservative Party in 2001

explanation.surface: A party leader who isn't leading, sweating as the election looms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A leader' looks generic, but it points to the then Tory leader, William Hague.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a malarial fever with bouts of shivering and sweating.

clue.text: Hard to understand thug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dense, weighty or difficult going
second meaning: as a noun, a hired tough or bruiser

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes dense, demanding material and is also slang for a bruiser hired to intimidate.

clue.text: Stupid sod in a giant woolly going in for a bustle creation

definitions.text: going in for a bustle creation

indicators.note: woolly means muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: git is British slang for a stupid person
taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot in a giant woolly costume trying out for a period-dress production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bustle' looks like the Victorian dress padding; here it means a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To be agitating is to stir people up, engaging in creating a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: TV time for the faithful Lord's crowd

parts.note: the Lord is God, so the possessive gives God's
a lot is a group or crowd of people

explanation.surface: Sunday television for believers set beside the crowd at Lord's cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, but here it is the Lord as God.
explanation.definitionFit: The God slot is British slang for the scheduled period of religious broadcasting on Sunday television.

clue.text: Colonel soundly fortified by delicatessen cereal

definitions.note: colonel is pronounced kernel, and a kernel is the core of something

indicators.note: the answer is held within the walls of the two words, like a fort

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A delicatessen cereal enriched with vitamins, with a colonel thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works through the sound: colonel is said kernel, and kernel means the heart of a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence and kernel both mean the central, most important part of something.
